transport.compatibility_expectation: External callers may depend on one request line producing one bounded JSON-RPC response line; invalid JSON and invalid params fail closed without exposing raw prompt, file, command, environment, path, or secret material.

compatibility_matrix.compatibility_expectation: May invoke and render bounded Runtime protocol results, but must not own runtime policy, permission, replay, recovery, workspace mutation, or completion decisions.
May validate and present bounded protocol shapes, but must not infer Runtime authority or make policy decisions.
May schedule explicit bounded Runtime commands, but scheduler, daemon, worker, lease, hosted isolation, metrics, and secret provider products are outside Runtime release readiness.

boundary_surfaces.title: Run Request
boundary_surfaces.compatibility_expectation: Requests must carry bounded objective or continuation identity, task/run handles, idempotency or expected fingerprints where required, policy fingerprints, scoped inputs, and secret references rather than secret values.

boundary_surfaces.title: Runtime Event
boundary_surfaces.compatibility_expectation: Events are append-only bounded evidence for runtime state, progress, permission, tool, approval, recovery, completion, refusal, and attestation; they must not persist raw prompt, provider response, file content, command, environment, path, or secret material.

boundary_surfaces.title: Control Command
boundary_surfaces.compatibility_expectation: Control commands must be explicit, caller-authorized where mutating, and checked against current run state, target fingerprints, and continuation identity so stale commands fail closed.

boundary_surfaces.title: Run Result And Attestation
boundary_surfaces.compatibility_expectation: Results expose bounded status, artifact references, verification results, runtime/Mode Pack/LLM/toolchain identifiers, policy fingerprints, ledger references, replay state, completion evidence, failure classification, and blocker/refusal reasons.

boundary_surfaces.title: Run Inspection
boundary_surfaces.compatibility_expectation: Inspection is read-only and summary-bounded; it derives from persisted Runtime state and must not execute work, append ledger events, or reveal raw sensitive material.

boundary_surfaces.title: Task Runtime
boundary_surfaces.compatibility_expectation: Task lifecycle, agent-loop execution, ledger writes, completion, refusal, recovery, replay, and terminal state transitions remain Runtime-owned and are only invoked through bounded protocol commands.

boundary_surfaces.title: CLI External Loop
boundary_surfaces.compatibility_expectation: The CLI starts or resumes bounded Runtime work through `brownie run` and `brownie resume`; it presents progress and results without reimplementing the agent loop or Runtime policy.

boundary_surfaces.title: VSIX Validation
boundary_surfaces.compatibility_expectation: VSIX validators mirror bounded Runtime protocol shapes for UI safety and drift detection, but do not own policy or grant Runtime authority.

non_authority: CLI and VSIX presentation cannot grant Runtime authority.
Protocol schemas and validators can narrow or reject, but cannot widen Mode Pack policy or Runtime permissions.
MCP descriptions, schemas, annotations, results, secret references, and executable identity remain non-authoritative.
Raw prompt, provider response, file content, command output, environment values, absolute paths, canonical paths, secret values, and executable content must not be durable boundary evidence.
